Definitions Content: Upper limb prostheses are devices that substitute a missing hand or limb to restore function and/or appearance. Source Title: A review of upper limb pediatric prostheses and perspectives on future advancements

Clinical Content: Reports high pediatric device abandonment and mixed evidence for functional benefit: higher abandonment rates in children than adults and studies showing no clinically relevant functional/QoL differences between wearers and nonwearers [9]. Notes clinical factors in prescription and use: psychosocial influences (self-image, social stigma, parental influence), physical functioning limits of devices, trade-offs between function and aesthetics, device weight, harness discomfort, maintenance/cost, growth-related fit issues, and need for training and intuitive control strategies [9]. Cites some evidence that body-powered devices may yield better task performance satisfaction in some cohorts [9].
Regulatory Content: Notes that clinically prescribed pediatric prostheses differ from experimental/3D-printed devices in that prescribed devices undergo rigorous engineering development and regulatory approvals before commercial availability [9]. Does not provide specific regulatory frameworks, classifications, standards, or safety/validation procedures beyond this distinction.
